subject: Output to engines other than pdf

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Output to engines other than pdf
parts:
Hi:

If a document is supposed to be processed with Xe(La)TeX or LuaTeX
rather than pdfLaTeX, is there a supported way to do that yet in
knitr? I couldn't find it in the docs or options, but I may have
missed something. I'm trying to see if one can use knitr with the
tikzDevice package to use a font that is defined in the fontspec
package of LaTeX and to be processed with xelatex. Nothing I need,
simply an experiment, but it has to do with a post on the ggplot2 list
last night.

TIA for any help,
Dennis

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Output to engines other than pdf
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure what you mean: what's wrong with running, say, xelatex
instead of pdflatex on knit's output .tex file? That's what I've been
doing all along, with custom fonts in the document

$ cat /usr/bin/knit
#!/usr/bin/Rscript
args <- commandArgs(TRUE)
library(knitr)

knit(paste(args, ".Rnw", sep=""))
system(paste("xelatex ", args, ".tex", sep=""))

Now, with device=tikz, tikzDevice also needs to know you'll use xetex
etc., some options are documented in ?setTikzDefaults such as
tikzLatexDefault and tikzXelatexPackages. I think they have an example
in the package vignette.

Cheers,

baptiste

Here's the example; the input file is pretty small:
##-------------- start ----------------
\documentclass[11pt]{article}

require('ggplot2')

DF <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)
ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
labs(x = 'My x-axis', y = 'My y-axis') +
opts(title = 'This is the title',
plot.title = theme_text(size = 14))
@

\end{document}

I'm on Windows, so no shell scripts :)

I should also load the tikzDevice package with knitr and ggplot2. I'll
chase this down and see where this leads.

Dennis

parts:
Perhaps the graphics manual is too long to read... sorry about my
boring writing :)
https://github.com/downloads/yihui/knitr/knitr-graphics.pdf (go to the
section on tikz) Once the tikzDefaultEngine option is set, knitr
should be able to do the rest of the job automatically.

BTW, thanks, Baptiste, for the hint on a bash script. I happen to have
a version too: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/bin/knit
My practice is to put such bin scripts under $HOME/bin and add this
path to the $PATH variable, so I do not have use sudo to modify it
every time. In fact I just created a symbolic link for the 'knit'
script from the knitr package to HOME.

Regards,

Hi:

I neglected to go through the graphics manual before I posted. I am shamed :p

I'm pretty new at xelatex so I undoubtedly skipped over that part of
the graphics manual when I read it a few weeks ago (the correct mantra
is on p.6). I was able to get a suitable .tex file (after commenting
out the \usepackage[xetex]{graphicx} line) with
knit('myplot.Rnw')

and then from a shell, xelatex myplot.tex. However, when I ran
knit2pdf('myplot.Rnw', 'myplot.tex')

I got a bunch of error messages, which culminated in the ominous

This is a fatal error: LaTeX will abort

I'm guessing xelatex and LuaTeX support are not built into knit2pdf()
yet. True/False/other? [I checked to be sure - I'm using knitr_0.2.3
in this session.]

Regards,
Dennis

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Output to engines other than pdf
parts:
knit2pdf() is not a proper tool to use in this case, because it is a
wrapper to texi2pdf() which uses pdflatex by default, so I would
suggest you run knit() first, then call xelatex manually. However, I
can certainly look into this issue so knit2pdf() can support xelatex
as well.

Regards,
Yihui

parts:
Ramnath Vaidyanathan helped me with this issue
(https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/131), and you can call
